judgements.reason: PadicMeasures only needs Iwasawa-algebra theory on top of Mathlib's AbstractMeasure/Amice/Weierstrass files (completed group rings, the Lambda-module structure theorem and characteristic ideals, determinant lines, Gorenstein duality, rigid weight spaces). ComputationalNumberTheory adds to its certified factorization, number-field and numerics layers the modular curves over Z with Hecke correspondences (R12-R14 with stacks R09 and GAGA C0-C5), SchemeAndStack SF.0-SF.3 and, through FF.2, the Weil conjectures and Deligne's weights, so it is much farther.

AdicSpaces already has Spv, Spa, rational subsets and the flatness chain in Tau Ceti; it still needs Tate acyclicity/Buzzard-Verberkmoes, adic spaces with gluing and the Fargues-Fontaine curve with Kedlaya's strong noetherianity of B^I. PadicMeasures must build seven layers from a thinner base (completed group rings and convolution, phi/psi, the Lambda-module structure theorem and characteristic ideals, determinant functors, Gorenstein orders), and its rigid weight spaces presuppose the unbuilt sheafiness and gluing of adic/rigid spaces, so it is slightly farther.

AdicSpaces is half built, and its remaining sheafiness, gluing and Fargues-Fontaine layers need no other roadmap. SchemeAndStack needs algebraic spaces and stacks, proper/smooth base change with compact support, Picard schemes and Jacobians, formal schemes and de Jong alterations, and Fulton-style intersection theory with GRR, far more new theory.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory must build the homotopy input (classifying spaces, Quillen A/B, plus construction, group completion, spectra), E0/E5 infinity-categorical basics, Matsumoto and Suslin's K_3, and then the Q- and S-constructions, localization, nonconnective K and products. SchemeAndStack starts from Mathlib's schemes but still needs algebraic spaces and stacks, etale base change and compact support (via the unbuilt CohomologicalPointCounting/EtaleDuality owners), Picard schemes, formal geometry with alterations, and intersection theory with GRR, which I judge somewhat larger.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory is the homotopy/infinity-categorical input plus Quillen-Waldhausen theory and classical low-degree K-theory. InverseGalois inherits SchemeAndStack SF.0-SF.3 (descent, stacks, etale cohomology, curves and Picard objects), GAGA and Chow algebraization (C0-C4) and Hilbert schemes/stacks (R09.1-R09.4), and adds pi_1 specialization, Riemann existence, Hurwitz spaces and Shafarevich's theorem (which also needs unbuilt class field theory and Galois cohomology), so it is somewhat farther.

CrystallineCohomology needs the infinity-categorical derived-sheaf and animation stack E0-E5, the cotangent complex and derived completion, and then PD envelopes, crystalline sites, finiteness and duality, de Rham-Witt, log-crystalline and Hyodo-Kato theory. InverseGalois needs SF.0-SF.3 with etale base change, stacks and Picard objects, GAGA and Riemann existence, Hurwitz spaces, and Shafarevich's theorem with class field theory and Poitou-Tate inputs, which I judge slightly larger.

CrystallineCohomology's closure is E0-E5, DD.0-DD.1, L-eta and Dieudonne theory under its own crystalline, de Rham-Witt, log and Hyodo-Kato layers. EllipticKTheory contains essentially all of GeneralAlgebraicKTheory (homotopy input, plus/Q/S constructions, Matsumoto, Suslin) and adds Thomason-Trobaugh K-theory of schemes with Adams operations, Tate's K_2 theorem with Poitou-Tate duality, Quillen finite generation via Borel-Serre and reduction theory, and Quillen's finite-field computation with Bott periodicity.

EllipticKTheory is a deep K-theory tower (GAK, Thomason-Trobaugh, arithmetic finite generation, Tate's K_2) with elliptic-curve applications. Heights needs SchemeAndStack SF.0-SF.5, Faltings' finiteness with Arakelov heights and Faltings-Chai compactifications of Siegel moduli, Neron models and finite flat group schemes, the p-adic comparison theorems behind R28.4, Poitou-Tate/Selmer descent, the subspace theorem, and Mordell-Lang and Bogomolov, a far larger stack (about 230 external stages against about 105).

Heights' closure already contains most of DiamondSixOperations' prerequisites (infinity-enhancements, perfectoid spaces, diamonds, prismatic/crystalline inputs, EDC, stacks) through the p-adic Hodge route to Faltings' theorem. DiamondSixOperations adds only ECD etale cohomology C0-C9, Huber's adic etale cohomology H0-H5 and the six operations, while Heights adds Shimura varieties and their compactifications, Arakelov geometry, Faltings, Neron models, A_inf and the comparison theorems, SF.0-SF.5, and Mordell-Lang/Bogomolov.

Every prerequisite and layer of PerfectoidQuotients (E0-E5, P0-P4, DD, PR.0-PR.2, CR.0-CR.2, Q0-Q4) lies inside DiamondSixOperations' closure. DiamondSixOperations adds diamonds and v-stacks D0-D6, perfectoid P5-P6, ECD etale cohomology C0-C9, Huber etale cohomology H0-H5, scheme etale duality, and its own Rf_!, Rf^!, cohomological smoothness and biduality.

CohomologyComparisons' closure contains all of PerfectoidQuotients (through AI.0). It adds A_inf cohomology AI.0-AI.6, nearly all of CrystallineCohomology (de Rham-Witt, log, Hyodo-Kato, duality), diamonds and relative Fargues-Fontaine geometry, prismatic PR.3/PR.6, p-adic period rings and sheaves, and its own comparison layers.

CohomologyComparisons needs the p-adic cohomology tower (A_inf, crystalline, prismatic, perfectoid, diamonds, period rings) plus its comparison layers. GeometricSatake shares much of that base and adds DiamondSixOperations S0-S5 with ECD and Huber etale cohomology, the scheme decomposition theorem with Weil II (EDC.0-EDC.7, DWP.0-DWP.9), v-stack/ULA sheaves, Bun_G and bundles on the curve, buildings and parahorics, and its own Grassmannian, convolution, fusion and Tannakian layers (about 205 against 98 closure stages).

GeometricSatake needs diamonds, six operations, Fargues-Fontaine geometry and Weil II under its Satake layers. RankZeroOneBSD's closure (about 620 stages) contains all of that except the Satake-specific stages and adds modularity of elliptic curves, Gross-Zagier, Heegner and Kato Euler systems, Iwasawa main conjectures, Shimura curves and Hilbert modular varieties, metaplectic forms and p-adic families.

RankZeroOneBSD's closure contains CohomologyComparisons CP.0 and CP.2-CP.4 and almost all their prerequisites (through Kato's reciprocity laws and automorphic Galois representations), and adds modularity, Gross-Zagier, Euler systems and main conjectures. CohomologyComparisons adds only CP.1, CP.5, CP.6 and two prismatic stages beyond it.

AdicSpaces is half built, and its remaining sheafiness, gluing and Fargues-Fontaine layers need no other roadmap. ComputationalNumberTheory needs certified-algorithm theory (factorization, number-field certificates, ball arithmetic) plus modular curves over Z with Hecke correspondences, stacks and GAGA, SchemeAndStack SF.0-SF.3, analytic L-function interfaces and, via FF.2, Weil/Deligne bounds.

Heights' closure contains SchemeAndStack SF.0-SF.5, since its height machine uses SF.5 intersection theory. On top of that it needs Faltings' finiteness with Arakelov theory and Siegel-moduli compactifications, p-adic Hodge comparison, Poitou-Tate/Selmer descent, the subspace theorem, and Mordell-Lang and Bogomolov.

GeneralAlgebraicKTheory is a single tower (homotopy input, Q/S constructions, low-degree K-groups). RankZeroOneBSD's closure has about 620 stages across 89 roadmaps: modularity lifting, Gross-Zagier, Euler systems, main conjectures and p-adic Hodge theory, and even part of GAK itself through Kato's Euler system.

GeometricSatake's closure contains DiamondSixOperations S0-S5 with all their prerequisites; only D6's biduality stage S6 is unused. On top of that it needs relative Fargues-Fontaine and Bun_G geometry, v-stack/ULA sheaves, Weil II and the decomposition theorem, buildings and parahorics, and its own Grassmannian, fusion and Tannakian layers.

PadicMeasures needs Iwasawa-algebra theory (completed group rings, the structure theorem, characteristic ideals, determinants, Gorenstein duality) and rigid weight spaces. InverseGalois needs SchemeAndStack SF.0-SF.3, GAGA and Chow algebraization, Hilbert schemes and stacks, pi_1 specialization, Riemann existence, Hurwitz spaces and Shafarevich's theorem, far more.

PerfectoidQuotients needs the infinity-enhancement and animation stack, cotangent complex and derived de Rham, perfectoid spaces with almost purity, prismatic cohomology with the Hodge-Tate comparison, and BS22 section 7. EllipticKTheory shares only E0/E5 and needs the full higher K-theory tower (homotopy input, Q/S constructions, Matsumoto, Suslin), Thomason-Trobaugh with Adams operations, Tate's K_2 theorem, Poitou-Tate, and Quillen finite generation via Borel-Serre and reduction theory, roughly three times as many stages of comparable depth.

CrystallineCohomology needs E0-E5, derived completion and the cotangent complex, and then crystalline sites, finiteness and duality, de Rham-Witt, log geometry and Hyodo-Kato. SchemeAndStack needs algebraic spaces and stacks, etale base change and compact support (through unbuilt etale owners), Picard schemes, deformation and formal geometry with alterations, and intersection theory with GRR; the two are close, and SchemeAndStack is slightly larger in breadth.

InverseGalois' external closure (SF.0-SF.3, GAGA C0-C4, stacks R09.1-R09.4) is contained in ComputationalNumberTheory's. On top of its algorithm layers, CN adds modular curves over Z with Hecke correspondences, abelian schemes, analytic L-functions and, via FF.2, Weil/Deligne etale theory, which outweighs IG's own pi_1, Riemann existence, Hurwitz-space and Shafarevich layers.

EllipticKTheory's closure contains GeneralAlgebraicKTheory's working stages and all their prerequisites. It adds K-theory of schemes (Thomason-Trobaugh, Gersten, Adams operations), Tate's K_2 theorem, Poitou-Tate duality, Quillen finite generation, and its own elliptic-curve K_0-K_3 and regular-model layers.

RankZeroOneBSD's closure contains DiamondSixOperations S0-S5 and all their prerequisites (through the endoscopic and decomposition-theorem inputs to Gross-Zagier); only D6's biduality stage S6 lies outside it. It adds hundreds of stages of modularity, Euler-system, main-conjecture and automorphic theory.
